case.question: Explain the difference between Type 1 and Type 2 faults on a PowerFlex 525 and provide an example of each.

key_points: Type 1 (Auto-Reset/Run) faults can be automatically reset if the fault condition clears; example: F002 Auxiliary Input
Type 2 (Non-Resettable) faults require drive or motor repair or wiring correction before the fault can be cleared; example: F006 Motor Stalled, F070 Power Unit failure
Type 1 faults show in the fault log but may not halt operation if auto-reset is enabled
Type 2 faults always halt the drive and require manual intervention to clear
wrong_if: States all PowerFlex 525 faults are Type 1 and can auto-reset within 30 seconds
Claims Type 2 faults only occur after the 100th power cycle
Confuses fault type with fault severity; a Type 1 fault may still indicate serious damage
Recommends ignoring any Type 1 fault as merely informational
